**Issue #2708 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2708: Patch: the dungeon run's leaderboards and run stats on the device
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

Part G of #2701, the dungeon run's stage 1: a `bot:fullsend` tree, so this part is built on the tree's integration branch and reconciled there. Its frozen spec is `docs/dungeon-run.md` DR14; the design it shows is DR9 (leaderboards and stats) of the same file.

The owner wants leaderboards and many stats, kept offline for now: the deepest floor reached, the most curses stacked, a score, and the fastest win. Every finished run is kept on the device as a `RunRecord` (part D writes them). This part is the page that ranks and shows them.

## The surface (frozen)

This part writes:

```ts
// apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.tsx, the page at /dungeon/stats (part D registers the route)
export function DungeonStats(): ReactElement;
```

It uses part D's `readRunHistory(): RunRecord[]` (`dungeon/store.ts`), as frozen in DR14, without waiting for it:

```ts
export type RunRecord = {
  seed: string; daily: boolean; mode: DungeonMode; curses: string[]; cursePoints: number;
  rowReached: number; won: boolean; score: number; embers: number; timeMs: number; endedAt: string;
  stats: RunStats;   // @jackioh/run: nodesVisited, fightsWon, elitesWon, ghostsWon, miniBossesWon, bossesWon,
                     // damageDealt, healingDone, cardsDrawn, turns, damageTaken, healed, coinsEarned, coinsSpent,
                     // ticketsEarned, ticketsSpent, cardsKept, cardsBought, cardsRemoved, cardsMadeRadiant,
                     // cardsBuffed, packsSkipped, artifactsTaken, artifactsLeveled, blessingsTaken, eventsSeen, chestsOpened
};
```

## What to do

- Four leaderboards over the history: the deepest row reached (`rowReached`), the most curse points (`cursePoints`), the top score (`score`) and the fastest win (the least `timeMs` among the runs won). Each ranks the top runs, with each run's seed, mode, date and whether it was a daily run.
- Filters: the mode (Sandbox, or Campaign, empty until stage 2) and daily runs only.
- An entry opens that run's stats: every `RunStats` field, labelled through `t()`, its time and turns, and its curses.
- An empty state for a device with no runs yet, linking to `/dungeon`, and a link back to `/dungeon`.
- Use test ids from `dungeon/stats/testids.ts`, prefixed `dungeon-`.

## Owns

`apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/`. No other part of #2701 edits it.

## Behaviors (proved by a vitest test whose comment names it, with a stubbed `readRunHistory`)

- **B32** The leaderboards on the device rank the deepest row, the most curse points, the top score and the fastest win, and each entry opens that run's stats.

## Done when

B32 is tested, the empty state and the filters included; `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` pass for this part's files.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `gpt` (codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41343182930)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Add the synchronous `/dungeon/stats` screen promised by DR14: four device-local leaderboards for deepest row, curse points, score, and fastest completed win, with Sandbox/Campaign and daily-only filters. Every ranked row will identify its run and open a complete, translated run-details dialog; a device with no history will get a clear way to start a run, and every state will retain a way back to `/dungeon`.

## Files to touch

| Path | Status | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.tsx` | new | Implement `DungeonStats`, synchronous history loading, deterministic filtering/ranking, four boards, empty/no-match states, and the complete run-details dialog. |
| `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/testids.ts` | new | Define the `dungeon-`-prefixed ids and leaderboard-key type used by the component and tests. |
| `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/dungeon-stats.css` | new | Give the page a one-screen responsive ledger layout and accessible modal using existing palette, type, surface, and hit-target tokens. |
| `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.test.tsx` | new | Stub `readRunHistory` and prove B32, both filters, fastest-win eligibility, complete details, and the device-empty navigation. |

Do not touch `apps/web/src/dungeon/store.ts`, route tables, `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json`, generated wire files, Rust crates, `spec/`, e2e, manifests/configuration, or forbidden bot/workflow paths; Parts B/D own those integration surfaces. No current SPEC section or ruling governs Part G yet: use `docs/dungeon-run.md` DR9 and frozen DR14 Surface/B32 as the design contract, plus CLAUDE.md rule 7 and `apps/web/README.md`; do not add a ruling.

## Steps

1. In `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/testids.ts`, export `DungeonLeaderboard = "deepest" | "curses" | "score" | "fastest"` and `dungeonStatsTestid`. Include ids for the root, mode select, daily-only checkbox, no-history and no-matches messages, each board and its empty-win message, a board entry keyed by leaderboard plus the record's original history index, the detail dialog/close control, detail metadata/time/curses, and a stat value keyed by `RunStats` field. Spell every returned string with the `dungeon-` prefix.

2. In `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.tsx`, import `RunStats` from `@jackioh/run`, `DungeonMode`, `RunRecord`, and `readRunHistory` from `../store.ts`, and the shared `EmptyState`, i18n number/date helpers, `paths`, `BackLink`, and modal-key helper. Add a typed, exhaustive `STAT_LABELS`/ordered-field definition for all 27 camel-case `RunStats` properties: `nodesVisited`, `fightsWon`, `elitesWon`, `ghostsWon`, `miniBossesWon`, `bossesWon`, `damageDealt`, `healingDone`, `cardsDrawn`, `turns`, `damageTaken`, `healed`, `coinsEarned`, `coinsSpent`, `ticketsEarned`, `ticketsSpent`, `cardsKept`, `cardsBought`, `cardsRemoved`, `cardsMadeRadiant`, `cardsBuffed`, `packsSkipped`, `artifactsTaken`, `artifactsLeveled`, `blessingsTaken`, `eventsSeen`, and `chestsOpened`. Keep English labels as data and call `t(label)` only while rendering so locale changes remain live.

3. In the same component file, add small local presentation helpers: mode/outcome/daily words through `t()`, the record date through `formatDateTime(new Date(endedAt), { dateStyle: "medium" })`, numbers through `formatNumber`, and elapsed `timeMs` as `H:MM:SS` (or `M:SS` below an hour) using named unit-conversion constants and zero-padding. Retain each record's original history index, filter without mutating the store's array, and explicitly break numeric-sort ties by that original index. Rank every matching record: `rowReached` descending, `cursePoints` descending, `score` descending, and only `won` records by `timeMs` ascending.

4. Implement `DungeonStats(): ReactElement` in `DungeonStats.tsx`. Read `readRunHistory()` once in a lazy `useState` initializer (no effect, promise, or loading state), default the mode select to `sandbox`, and add a `dailyOnly` checkbox that further limits the chosen mode. Render a one-screen tavern shell with `<BackLink to={paths.dungeon}>`, the filters, and: (a) the shared `EmptyState` with a `/dungeon` action when the unfiltered device history is empty; (b) one translated no-match message when history exists but the selected mode/daily combination has none; or (c) all four ordered leaderboards. Do not impose an unfrozen top-N cutoff. Each button row must show its rank/metric, seed, translated mode, formatted end date, and an explicit translated `Daily run` or `Not a daily run`; the fastest board shows its own translated no-winning-runs line when matching records exist but none were won.

5. Add an internal run-detail dialog in `DungeonStats.tsx`, opened by the shared entry-button renderer so entries on every board select the same original `RunRecord`. Give it `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, a labeled heading, and use `useModalKeys` so Escape, browser Back, and Tab follow the app's modal contract; close it from its Close button or only a click on the scrim, focus Close on open, and return focus to the opening entry. Show seed, mode, date, daily status, win/loss, `rowReached`, `cursePoints`, `score`, `embers`, formatted elapsed time, the stored curse strings (each through `t()`, or a translated `No curses`), and a definition list/table containing every field from the exhaustive stat definition, including `turns`, with translated labels and localized numeric values.

6. In `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/dungeon-stats.css`, import it from `DungeonStats.tsx` and lay out the filters and four boards as a responsive grid inside the shell's single `one-screen__body` scroll region. Make each full leaderboard row a button, use tabular numerals for ranks, metrics, dates, durations, and the details table, stack rows cleanly on a narrow phone, and make the detail body scroll inside a modal that fits the viewport. Use only the app's existing palette/semantic color, type-scale, radius, shadow, z-layer, motion, and `--hit-min` tokens; add no inline styles or raw replacement palette values.

7. In `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.test.tsx`, mock only `../store.ts`'s `readRunHistory` while retaining its types, build records through one fixture helper that supplies every `RunStats` field, reset mocks/DOM after each test, and include the `// B32` behavior comment. Keep assertions scoped through `dungeonStatsTestid`/accessible roles rather than CSS classes.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.test.tsx` — `it("B32 ranks the four device leaderboards and every entry opens the run's complete stats")`: stub three Sandbox records with deliberately different row, curse, score, win, and time values; assert each board's seed order, every row's mode/date/daily metadata, and that losses never enter fastest win, then open an entry from each board. For the selected run, assert the identifying metadata, formatted time, curses, and all 27 labeled stat values are present, then close before opening the next entry.
- `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.test.tsx` — `it("filters the boards by Sandbox or Campaign and by daily runs only")`: include daily/non-daily records in both modes, prove Sandbox is the default, switch the select to Campaign, toggle daily-only, and assert every rendered board contains only the expected original records; also prove a filter with no records shows the no-match state.
- `apps/web/src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.test.tsx` — `it("shows a device-empty state with ways back to Dungeon Run")`: stub `[]`, use the shared empty-state assertion, and verify both its action anchor and the top Back control target `paths.dungeon` while the synchronous reader was called once.
- Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.test.tsx`.
- Run `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`.
- Run `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/dungeon/stats`, then the issue's full lint gate `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e`.
- Run the repository gates required for this branch: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, and `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] `DungeonStats` reads device history synchronously and ranks all matching runs on all four requested metrics, with fastest win restricted to wins and stable ties.
- [ ] Sandbox/Campaign and daily-only filters work, including the intentionally empty Campaign/no-match state.
- [ ] Every leaderboard row includes seed, mode, date, and daily status and opens complete metadata, time, curses, turns, and all other `RunStats` fields.
- [ ] A device with no records has a shared empty state linked to `/dungeon`, and the page's Back control also returns there.
- [ ] All player-facing words and stat labels pass through `t()`, dates/numbers use the locale helpers, and every new test id starts `dungeon-`.
- [ ] The focused Vitest file, web typecheck, stats-directory/full requested ESLint checks, rustfmt, catalog, patches, and spec checks pass without changing generated or unrelated files.

## Risks

- Part D and the generated run types are absent on this branch today but are frozen dependencies. Import only the exact DR14 names (`RunRecord`, `DungeonMode`, `readRunHistory`, `RunStats`, and `paths.dungeon`) so reconciliation is mechanical; do not create fallback copies or widen another part's files.
- Sorting the array returned by the store in place would reorder shared history, and an unstated tie-breaker could make equal records jump. Rank copies carrying their original index and use that index only for deterministic ties and unique React/test keys, so duplicate seeds remain distinct.
- A loss with a short duration must not win the fastest board. Filter `won` before the ascending `timeMs` sort, while the other boards include finished wins and losses.
- The details view must not omit a stat when `RunStats` evolves. Make the label record exhaustive against `keyof RunStats`; TypeScript then points at this screen when the wire adds or removes a field.
- This page reads only completed `RunRecord`s that Part D intentionally stored on the device; it must not reach into a live run, engine state, practice worker, server, or hidden game information (CLAUDE.md rule 7). It does not affect replay determinism.
- Part D alone owns the Chinese dictionary under DR14. Keep this change inside `dungeon/stats/`; if reconciliation reveals a missing literal translation, add it to Part D's dictionary work rather than broadening Part G.
- `RunRecord.curses` contains strings but no `RunContent` lookup, and this screen is frozen as a synchronous history reader. Render those stored strings through `t()`; do not initialize a live dungeon or WASM content solely to recover a display name.

## Open questions

None. DR9/DR14 freeze the data and B32 behavior, and no new rules decision or human-only change is needed. The presentation choices are resolved here: show every matching record rather than invent a top-N limit; preserve device-history order on equal metrics rather than invent a date tie-break; default to Sandbox and offer exactly Sandbox/Campaign rather than add an unfrozen “all modes” choice; use one modal details view rather than invent a per-run route or repeat inline panels; display the stored curse strings rather than widen the frozen record or load run content; and display whole-second `H:MM:SS`/`M:SS` while still sorting fastest wins by exact `timeMs`, rather than expose raw milliseconds.
````
